entries.subject: Ortiz et al. (2017) occultation and lightcurve ellipsoid
entries.finding: The body uses the nominal solution's semiaxes of 1,161 × 852 × 513 km with the preferred pole at J2000 right ascension 285.1° and declination -10.6°; the README states this is an inferred shape, not a resolved mesh or a unique interior model.

entries.subject: Ortiz et al. (2017) equatorial ring geometry
entries.finding: The equatorial ring uses the same publication's 2,287 km radius and 70 km width; its gray and fixed opacity are schematic, it has no invented bands, it stays evenly lit and it uses no separate Shadows control.

entries.subject: Shared neutral gray for the unresolved surface
entries.finding: Replaced by the measured whole-disc colour. The gray was a display convention; published rotation-corrected colour indices and an occultation-based V geometric albedo now give Haumea a measured uniform colour (sRGB 188, 189, 191).
entries.revisitWhen: The published colour or albedo is withdrawn or shown not to describe the whole disc.

entries.subject: Disc-resolved images of Haumea
entries.finding: No usable resolved image exists. At about 50 AU the 2,322 km long axis spans about 0.06 arcsec, near the resolution limit of Hubble, JWST and Keck adaptive optics, which record Haumea and its moons as points; at about magnitude 17 it is too faint for VLT/SPHERE's visible-light correction. No spacecraft has visited. The angular size is computed from the Ortiz et al. (2017) axis and the distance, not taken from a paper.
entries.revisitWhen: A disc-resolved image or a flyby is published.

entries.subject: VLTI, SPHERE and NACO data in the ESO archive and the JMMC OiDB
entries.finding: Searched 2026-09-16 by object name (Haumea, 2003 EL61, 136108). The ESO raw archive holds SINFONI (80 frames), HAWK-I (88), WFI (341), FORS1 (26), EFOSC (9) and EMMI (1) observations from 2006 to 2013, and none from PIONIER, GRAVITY, MATISSE, AMBER, SPHERE or NACO. The OiDB returns no Haumea rows; the same query returns Polaris. The Betelgeuse and Polaris interferometric routes therefore have no input for Haumea.
entries.revisitWhen: Interferometric visibilities of Haumea are deposited, or an ELT instrument resolves its disc.

entries.subject: Public ALMA project 2022.1.01753.S on Haumea
entries.finding: The ALMA archive holds a public band 7 project on Haumea (target 136108_Haumea_2003_EL61; four observations on 2023-07-06; finest resolution 15.4 mas; principal author Csilla Kalup), missed by the earlier archive search, which did not include ALMA. The 2,322 km long axis spans about 64 mas at 50 AU, so about four beams: a thermal-emission image of that size would show the elongated disc, not a surface map. No resolved analysis of this project was checked, and the pipeline has no route that images ALMA visibilities.
entries.revisitWhen: A paper from project 2022.1.01753.S publishes resolved thermal images or maps, or the project's calibrated images are cast through the camera route.

entries.subject: Hubble frames of Haumea in MAST
entries.finding: MAST lists targets named Haumea or 2003 EL61 in HST programs 10860, 11169, 11518, 11971, 12004, 12037, 12243, 13873 and 18002 (WFPC2, NICMOS, STIS, COS and WFC3). The imaging pixels are about 0.04 arcsec (WFC3/UVIS) or coarser, against a disc of about 0.06 arcsec, so the frames record Haumea and its moons as points. Program 18002 (Proudfoot, cycle 33, observed March-April 2026, six-month proprietary period) is titled Probing the Interior of the Dwarf Planet Haumea; it is not surface imaging.
entries.revisitWhen: A published analysis extracts surface brightness structure from these frames.

entries.subject: Namaka passing in front of Haumea as an albedo-mapping route
entries.finding: When a moon crosses the primary, the brightness drop along its path measures the albedo of that strip, the method behind the first Pluto maps. HST program 12243 (Ragozzine, cycle 18) spent 10 orbits on a predicted Haumea-Namaka event in July 2010 (270 WFC3/UVIS frames). A 2026 review of trans-Neptunian mutual events says Haumea-Namaka attempts were hindered by uncertain predictions that prevented detection and interpretation; no albedo map has been published. The review's forward predictions were not checked for a new Haumea season.
entries.revisitWhen: A published analysis of the 2010 HST frames, or a new Haumea-Namaka event season with a reliable prediction.

entries.subject: Light curves and rotationally resolved spectra as a surface map
entries.finding: Disc-integrated data taken as Haumea spins constrain brightness or composition by rotational phase only: optical light curves (Lacerda 2010), Herschel thermal light curves (Santos-Sanz et al. 2017), VLT/SINFONI spectra from 2006 to 2013 (Gourgeot et al. 2016, spectral slope 1.45 +/- 0.82 % per 100 nm redder at the Dark Red Spot, no significant water-ice band difference) and JWST NIRSpec IFU spectra from program 1273 (March and July 2023). None gives latitude. Lacerda (2010) shows the spot's size and darkness are degenerate: from a few percent of the cross-section at about 20% of the surrounding albedo to a full hemisphere only 5% darker. A texture drawn from these would be one chosen model, not a measurement.
entries.revisitWhen: A published two-dimensional albedo or colour map of Haumea with stated uncertainties.

entries.subject: Rabinowitz et al. (2006) rotation-corrected BVRI colours
entries.finding: The weighted average of three nights (2005 January 25-27) after subtracting the rotational light curve, B-V 0.626 +/-0.025, V-R 0.343 +/-0.020, V-I 0.683 +/-0.020 (section 3.4, Table 3), gives the Color lens with the Ortiz et al. (2017) albedo through the disc-integrated-color method: linear sRGB 0.504, 0.511, 0.522, sRGB 188, 189, 191. Each colour uncertainty moves a channel by at most 2 of 255.

entries.subject: Ortiz et al. (2017) V geometric albedo of the main body
entries.finding: p_V 0.51 +/-0.02 from the occultation projected area and the main body's absolute magnitude sets the brightness of the Color lens. Its uncertainty moves every sRGB channel by 3 of 255.

entries.subject: MBOSS mean colours (Hainaut et al. 2012)
entries.finding: The MBOSS catalogue (J/A+A/546/A115) lists a three-epoch mean for Haumea of B-V 0.631 +/-0.025, V-R 0.370 +/-0.020, V-I 0.687 +/-0.020 from Jewitt et al. (2007, AJ 134, 2046), Rabinowitz et al. (2007, AJ 133, 26) and Trujillo et al. (2007, ApJ 655, 1172). Whether each epoch removes Haumea's rotational light curve is not verified; Rabinowitz et al. (2006) state that they subtract it, so their colours are used. Measured with the same method, the MBOSS values give sRGB 190, 189, 191.
entries.revisitWhen: A newer rotation-corrected colour set disagrees with Rabinowitz et al. (2006) beyond their uncertainties.

entries.subject: Thermal-model albedos from Herschel and Spitzer
entries.finding: Ortiz et al. (2017) cite earlier thermal albedos of 0.7-0.75 and 0.804 (+0.062/-0.095) and explain why the occultation size replaces them. Measured with the same method, 0.804 would give sRGB 230, 232, 234.
entries.revisitWhen: A thermal model that includes Haumea's elongated shape and ring disagrees with the occultation albedo.

entries.subject: The darker, redder region seen in Haumea's light curve
entries.finding: Lacerda (2010) models an asymmetry in the light curve as a region darker and redder than the mean surface. A uniform colour hides it. Its fitted size, latitude and contrast are not unique from the light curve and the display meridian is arbitrary, so it is not drawn.
entries.revisitWhen: A published surface map or rotationally resolved colour model fixes the region's extent and contrast in a body-fixed frame.

entries.subject: Ring and satellite light removed from the albedo
entries.finding: Ortiz et al. (2017) subtract 2.5% of the system brightness for the ring and about 11% for Hi'iaka and Namaka before computing p_V 0.51, and note the albedo would be smaller if those shares are larger. The published value is used unchanged.
entries.revisitWhen: A published albedo with separately measured ring and satellite contributions.

entries.subject: Retained JPL physical-primary state 920136108 at JD 2461286.5 TT
entries.finding: The prepared orbital position and conic use the pinned primary vector and validated epoch record shared with Hi'iaka, which replaced the older heliocentric conic in the prepared scene; the README says this is not a new long-term ephemeris.

entries.subject: Disagreeing middle-axis uncertainty in Ortiz et al. (2017)
entries.finding: The README records that the paper's main text and Methods give different uncertainties for the middle axis, 4 km and 2 km, while the nominal value agrees, so the adopted semiaxis is used with an unsettled error.
entries.revisitWhen: An erratum or a later publication settles the middle-axis uncertainty.

entries.subject: Absolute rotational orientation at the scene epoch
entries.finding: Known problems state that the pole is observationally constrained but the display meridian is arbitrary, because the measured 3.915341-hour period does not establish an absolute orientation at the application epoch; no fictitious rotational ephemeris is animated.
entries.revisitWhen: A published longitude system or absolute rotational ephemeris fixes Haumea's meridian at a known epoch.
